title: Projective morphisms are stable under base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a projective morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-projective-morphism] and let $g:S'\to S$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Form the fibre product $X':=X\times_S S'$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-base-change] and let $f':X'\to S'$ be its projection. Then $f'$ is projective [def-pc-projective-morphism].

source.place: Lemma Tag 01WF (morphisms-lemma-H-projective-base-change) together with Lemma Tag 01K5 (schemes-lemma-quasi-compact-preserved-base-change)

proof.text: By the definition of projective morphism [def-pc-projective-morphism], choose an integer $n$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ whose composite with the structural projection is $f$. Base changing this closed immersion along $g$ gives a closed immersion $i':X'=X\times_S S'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S\times_S S'$ by [lem-pc-closed-imm-base-change]. The canonical base-change identification $\mathbf P^n_S\times_S S'\cong\mathbf P^n_{S'}$ identifies the composite of $i'$ with the structural projection to $S'$ as $f'$. Thus $f'$ is H-projective.

The morphism $f'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], since $f$ is quasi-compact as part of the projective-morphism hypothesis. Combining this with the H-projective factorization from step 1 gives that $f'$ is projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism].
